result.question: Finance wants a number for Transformer 1 at site MAIN. If the gas trend means we'll need corrective oil work soon, how many hours and how much will it cost? Check whether hydrogen, ethylene and acetylene rose between 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 and 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000, give their daily rates in ppm/day, and project each forward 7 days from the last sample. If any projection crosses its IEEE C57.104 Condition 1 limit, treat corrective work as likely within the week. The limits are 100 ppm for hydrogen, 50 ppm for ethylene and 1 ppm for acetylene. Then look through the closed work order history on Transformer 1 for similar corrective jobs, such as oil treatment, degassing, filtration or internal inspection. Give me their average actual hours, average actual cost and average overrun versus plan, and use those to estimate the likely job. If corrective work is likely and no open work order already covers it, draft a work order carrying that estimate in the notes, and give me the MAIN site's overall backlog and overdue counts so I can see what it competes with. If no similar closed work orders exist, say so. In that case, base the estimate on the average of all closed Transformer 1 work orders and label it low-confidence. If none of the gases is projected to cross a limit, don't create a work order. Just report the estimate as a contingency figure.
result.answer:
I can't give Finance an hours or cost figure. Transformer 1 has no closed work orders at all, so there is nothing to average, not even as a low-confidence fallback. I also did not draft a new work order, because open work order 1000053 already covers this corrective outage.

**Gas trend.** The window end is exclusive, so there are 4 daily samples from 2024-01-15 to 2024-01-18. Daily rates are the change from first to last sample, divided by 3 days. Projections run 7 days from the last sample, to 2024-01-25.

| Gas | 01-15 | 01-18 | Rose? | Rate (ppm/day) | 7-day projection | Condition 1 limit | Crosses? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hydrogen | 2845 | 2900 | Yes | +18.33 | 3028.3 ppm | 100 | Yes (already ~29× the limit) |
| Ethylene | 16684 | 16600 | No (fell) | −28.00 | 16404 ppm | 50 | Yes (already ~332× the limit) |
| Acetylene | 7 | 7 | No (flat) | 0.00 | 7 ppm | 1 | Yes (already 7× the limit) |

The daily readings bounce up and down; hydrogen went 2845 → 2950 → 2800 → 2900. A least-squares fit gives hydrogen only about +1.5 ppm/day, so the rates are rough. That doesn't change the conclusion: all three gases are already far above their limits, and so are their projections. By your rule, corrective work is likely within the week.

**Closed work order history on Transformer 1.** There are no similar closed jobs (oil treatment, degassing, filtration or internal inspection). The asset has 3 work orders and none is closed:
- **1000051:** on-load tap changer inspection, PdM, priority 1, waiting for approval.
- **1000052:** confirmatory DGA oil sample, PdM, priority 1, waiting for approval.
- **1000053:** outage and inspection for 2024-01-20 to 21 (IEEE C57.104 Condition 4), corrective, priority 1, waiting for approval.

That leaves no actual hours, actual cost or overrun history to average.

**Work order decision.** Corrective work is likely, but I did not draft one:
- Work order 1000053 is already an open corrective outage and inspection work order raised on the same gas readings. A new one would duplicate it.
- There is no estimate to put in the notes.

If you want oil treatment or degassing written into 1000053's scope, or a separate work order anyway, tell me. It could only carry a "no historical basis" note.

**MAIN site workload (last 3 months).** Backlog is 3 and overdue is 0. All three backlog items are the Transformer 1 work orders above.

To get Finance a figure, you'll need a vendor quote or a site-standard estimate for transformer oil processing, since there's no internal history to use.
